correctness.rationale: The joint hit-conditioned law is flat in signed offset and spherical surface area, not flat in the direction marginal. At each generic endpoint let P=product |u_i|. The cap has volume h^d/(d! P), so its perpendicular base has area h^(d-1)/((d-1)! P). For small thresholds the two offset intervals are exactly of length ((d-1)! P t)^(1/(d-1)); evenness and Brunn concavity exclude an interior component. More importantly, the same concavity compares each offset on its half to the center: if r=min a_i/2 and W=||a||_2, inward depth is at most W t^alpha/(2 r omega_(d-1)^alpha) on the event. This dominates even near nongeneric normals and justifies the limit for bounded marked tests. The hemisphere moment of product |u_i|^alpha is Gamma((1+alpha)/2)^d/Gamma(d(1+alpha)/2); that of |u_j| is pi^((d-1)/2)/Gamma((d+1)/2). Their ratio with the two endpoints gives the stated constant, including 1/(a_1+a_2) in dimension two. The tilt of the squared coordinates adds alpha/2 to each Dirichlet parameter, sign reflections give a uniform independent contact vertex, and dividing the endpoint depth by its cutoff gives Uniform(0,1), whose (d-1)st power yields the beta mark. The same domination sends the conditional nonsimplex probability to zero. AM–GM is strict except for the cube. Facet-support offsets can have positive geometric area, but the record’s zero convention there concerns a null event and changes no law. The frozen verifier was read, not executed; its inclusion–exclusion area formula is the derivative of the truncated box cap volume and the checks are supplementary.
